author: A

components.title: Core spiral traversal algorithm
components.what: Implement the boundary-shrinking (top/right/bottom/left) loop that walks a non-empty rectangular matrix and appends elements in clockwise spiral order, correctly handling odd single remaining row or column without duplicating elements.

components.title: Empty/degenerate input handling
components.what: Guard for matrix == [] or matrix == [[]] (or all rows empty) and return [] immediately before entering the traversal loop, avoiding index errors on empty row/col bounds.

components.title: Assertion check against visible examples
components.what: Confirm the final code block, when run standalone, satisfies both given asserts (3x3 and 2x2 cases) plus sanity-check a 1xN and Nx1 case mentally since those are common hidden-test edges for spiral problems.

log.author: B

challenges.problem: Untested code: no test is provided for a non-square rectangle (e.g., 2x3 or 3x2). The visible examples are both square. The loop logic may break or skip elements for rectangles where one dimension is exhausted before the other.

Unsupported inference: the second guard `if top <= bottom and left <= right` is evaluated after `bottom -= 1` in the third loop. If the matrix has only one remaining row after the top traversal, the bottom row traversal may have already consumed it, but the left column traversal could still run and append duplicates or out-of-order elements.

Missing source: the condition `if not matrix or not matrix[0]` assumes all rows are non-empty if the first row is non-empty, but the prompt says 'a matrix of empty rows' which could mean rows like [[],[]] where matrix[0] is empty. This is covered, but a matrix like [[1,2],[]] is not valid per the prompt's 'equal-length row lists' constraint, so this may not be an issue.
